title: Far Side Moon Rocks Help Explain the Moon's Two Faces
summary:
The side of the Moon that faces Earth looks very different from the side that always faces away. Now scientists in China think they have found new clues that help explain why.

The near side has huge, dark plains made of cooled volcanic rock called basalt. The far side is mostly old, rough highlands covered in craters, with a much thicker crust. Scientists have argued for decades about what caused this difference.

In 2024, China's Chang'e-6 mission became the first to bring back rock samples from the Moon's far side. A team led by Professor Hejiu Hui of Nanjing University studied the chemistry of those rocks. They compared them with rocks from the near side collected by the Apollo missions and China's Chang'e-5 mission.

The team found something surprising. Deep inside the Moon, in a layer called the mantle, the material on both sides seems to be very similar. But the crust, the Moon's outer layer, is clearly different. Far side rocks held more of the element magnesium and very small amounts of rare earth elements.

The researchers suggest an explanation. Long ago, the young Moon was covered by an ocean of melted rock, called a magma ocean. At first, it cooled evenly. Later, the Moon became "tidally locked," meaning the same side always faced Earth. At that time, Earth and the Moon were much closer together. Earth's gravity pulled on the Moon and created more heat on the near side than on the far side.

According to the team's model, this uneven heating stirred huge flows of hot, melted rock inside the Moon. Over time, those flows helped give the Moon its two very different faces.
why_it_matters: Understanding why the Moon has two faces helps scientists learn how the Moon formed and changed, and how Earth's gravity shaped its closest neighbor.

keywords.explanation: Basalt is a dark rock that forms when hot lava cools and hardens.
The crust is the hard, rocky outer layer of a planet or moon.
The mantle is the thick layer of rock that lies under the crust.
Rare earth elements are a group of metals that scientists use to learn how rocks formed.
A magma ocean is a huge layer of melted rock that covered a young planet or moon.
Tidally locked means one side of a moon always faces the planet it circles.

background_read: The Moon spins exactly once each time it circles Earth, so the same side always faces us and the far side can only be seen by spacecraft.
Scientists learn how the Moon formed by studying the chemistry of its rocks, which can show where the material came from and how it cooled.
Most Moon rocks studied in labs came from the near side, collected by the Apollo missions and China's Chang'e-5 mission.
China's Chang'e-6 mission was the first to bring back samples from the far side, letting scientists compare both halves directly.
